source.stem:
The diagram shows a solid in the shape of a triangular prism.
AC = 5 cm, BC = 4 cm and CD = 7 cm.
Angle ABC = 90°.

parts.text: What does the word prism tell you about the solid in the diagram? [1]
Calculate the volume of the prism. Give the units of your answer. [4]
On the 1 cm² grid, complete the net of the prism. Two faces have been drawn for you. [3]
Calculate the surface area of the prism. cm² [2]

intelligence.enrichment: A solid's visible profile depends on the viewpoint, so the same solid can have different outlines from different viewpoints and a requested outline may be produced by more than one possible solid.

spec.instruction: Write one new grades 6 Mathematics question. Chapter: math/grade_08/ch_204. The student must decide: Decide which profile a solid can show from a chosen viewpoint, and whether more than one solid can fit the same profile condition. Use an Indian school or home setting and Indian names. Keep the source language register. Change the numbers, materials, or everyday situation. Do not copy the source stem. Recalculate the key. If the stem numbers activities 1..n, every number must appear in an option (or in a structured part's first-class options).
